name: semantic-retry
description: The ticket 11.4 canonical semantic-retry workflow (ADR-013). A `draft` llm step carries a validation chain (a `contains` validator requiring the marker `APPROVED`) plus a semantic policy: `max_attempts: 3` and a `feedback` template. On a failing verdict the engine rebuilds the prompt from the critique — the `${{ feedback.* }}` tokens splice in the semantic-attempt number, the rejected output, and the verdict issues — and re-attempts under a semantic budget disjoint from the transport retry budget; the augmented prompt re-keys the response cache by construction, so a semantic retry is never served a stale hit. Exhausting the three attempts dead-letters the step with the full verdict history; a passing verdict flows the approved draft into the downstream `publish` step. The two budgets are visible per step in the run status API as `transport_failures` and `validation_failures`, and each augmented prompt is stored on its attempt as `attempts[].feedback`. It runs against the offline mock provider (model `mock/sim-1`); swapping the model id for a real provider makes it a live self-correcting workflow unchanged.

config.prompt: Write a short launch blurb and end it with the word APPROVED once it is ready.
